subject: Clarification on latency budgets, SLO measurement window, and metrics exports
messages:
From: Samantha Ruiz <samantha@fintegrity.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@fintegrity.com
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLOs - latency definition, sampling window, and export API

Hi Alex,

Thanks for sending over the draft SLO language in the RFP response. Procurement had a few follow-ups we need clarified before our legal and SRE teams complete the checklist:

1) Latency SLOs — when you state p95 and p99 latency budgets, can you confirm whether those are measured at the platform edge (ingress) or after the model runtime (eg, includes model decode and streaming)? Do you count client retries toward the distribution?

2) Measurement window — is the SLO computed over a rolling 30-day window, calendar month, or a different cadence? If rolling, what is the sampling cadence for the window (per minute, per second aggregation)?

3) Maintenance & partial outages — how are scheduled maintenance windows accounted for? Is there an exception path for planned maintenance and emergency maintenance?

4) Alerting & paging — what thresholds trigger P1 vs P2 alerts for latency and availability, and who is on-call for Dedicated vs Hosted customers?

5) Metrics access — we need a technical mechanism to ingest raw metrics into our observability stack. Do you provide a metrics export API or scheduled CSV/JSON dumps? What retention do you offer for per-request traces?

6) Evidence for procurement — in the event of an exception request or dispute, what artifacts will you share (aggregated histogram, raw sample export, Grafana read-only invite)?

Can you provide a concise point-by-point response and any suggested wording we can include in the SLO appendix? We have a target to finalize terms by next Thursday.

Thanks,
Samantha Ruiz
Senior Procurement Manager
Fintegrity

--
Fintegrity Procurement Team

From: alex_martinez@redwood.com

Subject: Re: SLOs - latency definition, sampling window, and export API

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear questions. Quick answers first, then I'll loop in Ops for a short artifact packet: 

1) Latency measurement: p95 and p99 are computed on end-to-end request latency measured at the platform ingress (time request received by our API gateway to last byte sent to the client). This includes model token generation time and any queuing inside the inference runtime. Client-side retries are excluded from the primary SLO calculation; we dedupe by request id and measure successful attempts. Retries are visible in separate telemetry.

2) Windowing & sampling: we compute rolling SLOs over a 30-day sliding window with 1-minute aggregation buckets (histogram counters per minute). Percentiles are calculated over the aggregated distribution of those 1-minute buckets. We also produce calendar-month snapshots for billing/contract milestones.

3) Maintenance: Planned maintenance windows (announced >=72 hours, documented in the Console) are excluded from the SLO denominator if customers opt into the maintenance carveout; emergency maintenance is not excluded unless a formal exception is approved by both parties. Our procurement packet includes an exception-request workflow.

4) Alerting: Standard hosting customers receive automated alerts at p95 > budget for 15 continuous minutes (P2) and p99 > budget for 5 continuous minutes (P1). For Dedicated customers we can tailor thresholds; on-call rotations and escalation playbooks are part of the Dedicated onboarding.

5) Metrics access: we provide: (a) read-only Grafana invites for dashboards, (b) a metrics export API (REST endpoint) that returns time-series and per-bucket histogram payloads (JSON), and (c) scheduled CSV dumps (daily or weekly) by request. Per-request traces are retained 90 days by default; aggregated histograms are retained 13 months.

6) Evidence: For disputes we share aggregated histograms, minute-level raw samples (JSON) for the disputed window, and a read-only dashboard snapshot. Raw PII-free request payloads are only shared under an executed data-sharing addendum.

I'll attach a one-page SLO appendix and a suggested clause for the maintenance carveout. Marissa & Priyom — can you confirm the per-request retention window and whether we should offer a longer retention option for enterprise customers (and a price)?

Best,

Hi Samantha — appreciate the patience. Below is a consolidated response and the artifacts we promised. I’ve attached the one-page SLO appendix and a short process doc describing exception requests. High level point-by-point below, and I noted where the attachment has verbatim language you may paste into the contract: 

1) Latency measurement
- Measure point: platform ingress (time at our API gateway) to last byte sent to client; includes model runtime and network egress from our edge.
- Retries: client retries are excluded from SLO buckets when a request_id is present; unsuccessful retries are tracked separately in a retry metric.

2) Windowing & sampling
- We compute a rolling 30-day window using 1-minute aggregation buckets. Percentiles (p95/p99) computed on the 30-day distribution of those buckets. Calendar-month snapshots available on request for billing.

3) Maintenance carveouts
- Planned maintenance (>=72 hours notice) is excluded from the SLO denominator if the customer elects the maintenance carveout. Emergency maintenance is subject to exception review; wording and workflow are in the attached process document.

4) Alerting & on-call
- Hosted: P2 at sustained p95 breach for 15m; P1 at sustained p99 breach for 5m.
- Dedicated: thresholds are negotiable; dedicated customers get a named on-call rotation and an escalation path.

5) Metrics & exports
- We offer: read-only Grafana invites; a metrics export REST API (minute- and bucket-level JSON payloads); and scheduled CSV dumps (daily/weekly). Default per-request trace retention: 90 days. Enterprise add-on: 365-day retention available for an incremental fee (pricing attached).

6) Evidence for disputes
- Provided artifacts: aggregated histograms for the disputed window, minute-level raw samples (JSON), read-only dashboard snapshot. Raw request payloads require a data-sharing addendum.

Attachments included: slo-definition-diff.xlsx (contains suggested contract text and examples), metrics-access-proposal.pdf (details on API endpoints and retention SLAs).

If this looks good, Samantha, we can (a) provide the Grafana invite and a test API token within 24 hours, and (b) include the maintenance carveout language in the next statement of work. Let me know which retention option you prefer for trace exports and whether your SRE team wants a short walk-through session.
